Reference / http/static

http/static#

Files from a directory, with validators, ranges and precompressed variants.

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

let files = StaticFiles(root: FileRoot(Directory(Path("public"))), media: StandardMediaTypes(), policy: StaticPolicy());
Route(method: Method.get, pattern: RoutePattern("/assets/*file"),
    handling: StaticFiles(root: root, media: types, policy: StaticPolicy(), random: SecureRandom(),
        clock: SystemClock(), parameter: "file"));

Description#

Files from a directory, with validators, ranges and precompressed variants.

Paths never leave the root: each name is opened below it without following links. Responses carry ETag and Last-Modified, answer conditional and range requests, and serve .br or .gz companions when the policy allows. By default index.html is the index, there is no listing, at most 16 ranges and 1024 names per directory. web/routing's Files is the usual way in.

Public API#

object StaticPolicy#

object StaticPolicy

Policy is immutable; the supplied root is borrowed. Every selected response owns an independent descriptor. No joined request path or stat/open pair.

StaticPolicy.StaticPolicy#

StaticPolicy()

index.html, no listing, no companions, 16 ranges, 1024 names, no Cache-Control, metadata ETags.

object StaticFiles#

object StaticFiles does Handling

Files below root, answered with validators, ranges and optional precompressed companions. The request path names the file, or, with parameter:, the route parameter of that name does (a final wildcard, #107):

Route(method: Method.get, pattern: RoutePattern("/assets/*file"),
    handling: StaticFiles(root:, media:, policy:, random:, clock:, parameter: "file"))

StaticFiles.file_response#

The response for the file at path below root, as a GET of request asks for it (validators and ranges), with the Date of now: web/reply's FileReply (#82). A missing file is 404, a bad path 400.

enum FileTags#

enum FileTags = (metadata, content)

How a file's ETag is made (#109): metadata from its identity, size and times (the default, cheap, different on each replica), content from its bytes (read once per version of the file, the same on every replica).
